races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Race

runners_data.name: Crayons In The Sky
runners_data.comment: A St Mark's Basilica breeze-up purchase at €80,000, she is a half-sister to See That Storm, a smart performer over longer trips, out of a dam effective at 7f; intriguing pedigree but debut winners here are uncommon and she looks an unlikely debutant.

runners_data.name: Scandi Noir
runners_data.comment: A very promising debut when third at Cork 17 days ago, giving a significant first-run advantage to the leaders and still beaten only two and a quarter lengths; she shapes as a filly with more to offer if produced with greater urgency, and 6f on good ground suits.

runners_data.name: Cyclone Code
runners_data.comment: Beaten seven lengths on debut at Roscommon and now off a 51-day break, he is bred for a longer test around 7f and this 6f trip may not be ideal; likely to find this level testing but improvement remains possible from limited experience.

runners_data.name: Anglesea Bridge
runners_data.comment: A Soldier's Call colt from a yard that prepares debutants well, he comes from a staying dam but his sire's speed should mean 6f is within range; an interesting profile with a top yard behind him, though debut form is inherently uncertain.

runners_data.name: Alwaysanangel
runners_data.comment: A 75,000 guineas breeze-up purchase by Harry Angel and a full-sister to Yorkshire, a smart 7f performer, she comes from a yard with an excellent record with first-time starters; a tongue-tie is fitted and she looks a likely type to make an immediate impact.

runners_data.name: Arrowstock
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on debut at Navan when eight lengths off the pace, she has speed in her pedigree and should learn from that initial experience; drawn wide from stall 9 and hard to fancy to win here but some improvement can be expected.

runners_data.name: Away And Gone
runners_data.comment: A better showing when fourth at Navan last time, beaten five and a quarter lengths down in class, she was highly regarded on debut and looks capable of taking another step forward now tried over this longer trip; speed in her pedigree and a legitimate threat.

runners_data.name: Ivory River
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in an auction event here on her only start to date, she carries a first-time visor and is drawn wide, though her pedigree carries speed and limited experience makes improvement possible; the trainer is out of form and she has much to prove.

runners_data.name: Pink Venom
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a maiden at Leopardstown on her only start, she comes from a capable yard but has everything to prove at this level; some speed in her pedigree offers a slim basis for optimism but a big step forward is required.

races.name: Dino Day At Fairyhouse On July 8th Apprentice Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: I'm Spartacus
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 5yo in top form (won 6f Fairyhouse last time, 1/6f/GOO) for an in-form McGuinness yard (T14: 3/28); 6f on good ground is squarely in his wheelhouse and a 19-day turnaround suits.|
runners_data.comment: Won here by two and a half lengths off a lower mark on his penultimate start; he was below his best in sixth last time and inconsistency is his main risk, but the course suits and 6f is his trip.

runners_data.name: Tawaazon
runners_data.note: Hold-up 8yo returning to 6f after a 7f spin on soft, with a best recent run of 2/5f/GOO; headgear (tongue-tie) suggests needs plenty of room, and the overloaded rear means getting a clear run is far from certain.|
runners_data.comment: Back to his best just seven days ago when a narrow second at a stiff track on a reduced trip off a mark 2lb lower, he holds solid course-and-distance form and looks well placed on this evidence; first-time tongue-tie and blinkers.

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Paul Flynn but form figures of 90090 paint a bleak picture; 5yo has failed to finish in the first four on his last five starts and a 28-day break doesn't obviously spark revival — carry lightly.|
runners_data.comment: Well held in his last five starts, beaten heavily without clear excuse at the Curragh last time, he does drop below his previous best mark here and the first-time tongue-tie and blinkers add an interest; effective on this going over this trip.

runners_data.name: Lady Kelly
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for the Murtagh yard (T14: 7/33) who is essentially a pace-setter on a flat track, but her tendency to fade in the finish and very limited form at 6f (all recent starts at 7f+) are significant liabilities down the straight.|
runners_data.comment: A narrow third at Down Royal 12 days ago having done too much in front early, she showed genuine ability on that evidence and could benefit from a more patient approach; the trainer is in good form and first-time blinkers are applied.

runners_data.name: Rosato
runners_data.note: Prominent 5yo for Charles Weld; not without ability (3/6f/HEA) but recent 6f Fairyhouse runs of 7th and 12th suggest this track/distance combination doesn't always bring out the best, and the yard is quiet (T14: 0/2).|
runners_data.comment: Drawn at one end of this large field, she missed the start last time and was unable to land a blow when beaten eight lengths here; drops below her previous best mark and suits stiff tracks over this trip, but a more positive display is needed.

runners_data.name: Tara Na Ri
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Noel Meade stepping well down in trip from 8f-10f territory; fades in the finish flag is a concern, and there is no meaningful 6f form to draw on — the trip looks too sharp.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten nine lengths here last time when dropping in class, he is a 10f horse likely to find this 6f trip a stiffer challenge; drawn at one end of this sizeable field and has much to prove at this level.

runners_data.name: Love Bomb
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3yo wearing a visor; has shown a snippet of ability (4/5f/STA) but flat-track 6f Fairyhouse is a new test and the fade flag plus modest recent figures (0 from last 6) make the case unconvincing.|
runners_data.comment: Hampered by a slow start at Gowran Park last time and beaten six lengths without getting competitive, a stronger beginning is essential here; she has shown her best form over 5f and the first-time visor arrives as connections look to spark a turnaround.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two second-place finishes in recent starts (2/6f/GOO, 2/5f/SOF); lightly-weighted 5yo who could feature if travelling smoothly just off Lady Kelly — one of the more interesting unexposed profiles in the prominent group.|
runners_data.comment: In solid form over recent months, twice runner-up in his last four starts, though he pulled too hard in front and was beaten four lengths off this mark last time; effective at 5-6f on any going and worth another chance here.

runners_data.name: Hero Of The Hour
runners_data.note: Veteran 9yo wearing a visor; prominent racer who has hit the frame at 6f on STA and has a win at 6f on good — big field experience is a plus, though age and modest OR=48 limit ambitions.|
runners_data.comment: Below his best when outpaced over an inadequate trip at Naas last time, his prior form was sound and stepping back up in distance should bring out a better effort; the first-time visor is an interesting aid, though the wide draw from stall 17 is a challenge.

runners_data.name: Step Back In Time
runners_data.note: Prominent 8yo who won 6f/GOO (1/6f/GOO) within recent form and has multiple place efforts; cheekpieces fitted, lightly-raced this term, and Chris Timmons' yard (T14: 0/0) is quiet — but the course/distance form is the standout positive.|
runners_data.comment: A front-runner by preference who won at this course and over this distance previously, she was poorly positioned and beaten nine lengths here last time; drops back below her winning mark and first-time cheekpieces arrive, though she needs to rekindle that earlier form.

runners_data.name: Mini Cotai
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3yo fitted with hood and tongue-tie; best effort recently 2/5f/SOF, and 6f is slightly further than ideal — will need to be delivered from a position that may not be available given the congested hold-up sector.|
runners_data.comment: An exposed maiden but in decent enough form, she shaped as if in need of a stronger test at Naas last time, beaten three and a quarter lengths off a mark 7lb below today's; a first-time tongue-tie is fitted and 6f on this ground suits her.

runners_data.name: Monastere
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose natural position is at the rear, placed here in midfield only because the back of the field is oversubscribed; showed ability with a 2nd on 6f/GOO but the style-fit penalty (0.90) means the race shape works against him.|
runners_data.comment: A better run last time when a positive ride suited and he was beaten three and a half lengths here, showing this trip and course agree with him; needs to build on that effort but his wider recent record offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Clarabell
runners_data.note: Returning from a 458-day absence for McGuinness; a true hold-up horse slotted into midfield due to the crowded rear — the layoff alone makes this an extremely risky proposition regardless of positional issues.|
runners_data.comment: Returning after an absence of over a year, she had little to show from her recent starts and finished well down the field at Leopardstown on her most recent outing; first-time tongue-tie fitted but much is needed here.

runners_data.name: Jackandthefox
runners_data.note: Prominent 7yo with sound 6f form (5/6f/GOO, 4/6f/GOO) and two place efforts on similar ground; a quiet yard (T14: 0/3) but the horse races to type and has the course distance profile to factor.|
runners_data.comment: Had his chances at Fairyhouse last time and was beaten five and a quarter lengths, showing this trip is within his range; a frustrating sort who has been difficult to get right, though he has ability on his day and the 5-6f trip suits.

runners_data.name: Livingston Range
runners_data.note: Veteran 8yo hold-up horse wearing a tongue-tie, placed into midfield because true hold-up spots are at a premium; his two 4th-place finishes on 6f/GOO show he can get competitive but the style-fit score of 0.92 signals he's likely racing out of role.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Naas last time when unable to keep up over a shorter trip, he is on an extended losing sequence and has shown inconsistency; a first-time tongue-tie arrives and 5-6f on good going is his ground, but he needs to find more.

runners_data.name: Run Forrest Run
runners_data.note: Hold-up 8yo whose entire recent form is at 7f, not 6f — the drop in trip is untested and he has been redistributed to midfield, meaning he won't operate from his favoured position; both factors combine to make this a very difficult task.|
runners_data.comment: Engaged in a pace duel at Limerick last time and beaten over eight lengths as a result, he has been struggling for form throughout recent starts; drawn wide from stall 16 and needs to switch off to be a factor.

runners_data.name: Glen Breeze
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 3yo with a recent 2/6f/GOO catching the eye, fitted with cheekpieces and a tongue-tie; despite the hold-up redistribution (style-fit 0.90) this is arguably the most interesting runner forced out of its natural position — the form figures hint at more than the map suggests.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten over nine lengths here last time without any clear mitigation, he finds his mark more lenient than usual but his penultimate effort was better and inconsistency has been a theme; effective over 6f and with more to offer if he finds his form.

runners_data.name: She's On The Ball
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3yo for Laura Hourigan with a fade tendency and no finish better than 5th in recent starts; 6f on good is fine in theory but three consecutive single-figure finishes (0005) offer little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Shaped a little better than her recent record suggests when a respectable fifth at Limerick last time, beaten four lengths; she has yet to find her ideal conditions and faces the widest draw from stall 18, with more improvement needed to be competitive.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Kelly is the sole confirmed front-runner and will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the gates on this flat Fairyhouse 6f, with no serious rival expected to challenge her for the lead — her history of fading in the finish is the key vulnerability. The prominent brigade of I'm Spartacus, Rappell, Rosato, Whatswrongnow, Hero Of The Hour, Step Back In Time, and Jackandthefox will settle just off the pace and be best positioned to pounce if Lady Kelly ties up in the final furlong. The field holds considerably more hold-up and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Glen Breeze, Monastere, Run Forrest Run, and Livingston Range are genuine hold-up horses but are mapped to midfield because the rear is oversubscribed, meaning they will not operate from their natural position and their finishing kicks may be blunted. The race shape — a single front-runner setting a manageable tempo — strongly favours prominent racers travelling close to the pace, who can collar Lady Kelly in the final furlong without needing an extended run from deep.

watchPoints.text: Lady Kelly's sectionals — if she is allowed to bowl along unchallenged in the first two furlongs, the race turns into a test of whether the prominent pack have enough boot to run her down in the final 100 yards; watch her early splits.

I'm Spartacus drew well and won over this exact course and distance last time — any signs of a forward move entering the final furlong should be treated seriously given the pace dynamic that puts him perfectly placed.

Glen Breeze is a redistributed hold-up type with recent form of 2/6f/GOO; if he can manoeuvre closer than his natural position and finds daylight in the straight, his unexposed profile could surprise at a big price.

Step Back In Time's cheekpieces application is worth noting given the OR drop to 47 — small headgear changes for Chris Timmons can sometimes sharpen a horse's early response in a race where prominent position is the currency.

The volume of hold-up horses (six-plus) crammed into midfield means there will be significant traffic and switching in the final 2f — watch for horses who find trouble in running or take wide routes, as the clean-run premium will be unusually high.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Tropical Retreat
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner from the Thomas Mullins yard; Colin Keane takes the ride and she has a good-to-firm course win on her CV, but the 243-day absence is a significant flag and the style-fit score of 0.93 reminds that she is capable of racing off this pace rather than from the front — watch the market for evidence she has come back ready.
runners_data.comment: Off the track for over eight months and facing a significant fitness question on her comeback, she encountered trouble at the start of her most recent outing which disrupted her run. A notable jockey booking provides interest, but her current figures trail the pace-setters in this field.

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan partners a filly who is genuinely a prominent racer by nature, yet with more pace-seeking types than positions available she has been absorbed into midfield on the map — her recent run just four days ago and a sim-going record of 0W4P in 14 comparable starts suggest she may find the race shape unkind rather than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Won at Leopardstown this season and handles today's conditions; she ran to her mark last time despite racing excessively keen in a tougher test. First-time cheekpieces applied for today's quick turnaround — just four days between runs — and the mark looks fairly assessed.

runners_data.name: Treasure Rose
runners_data.note: In excellent form (23-221) for the powerful J P Murtagh yard, which is firing at 7/33 over 14 days; Ben Coen rides a filly who is a natural prominent type genuinely in role here, boasts a strong good-going record, and steps back to six furlongs after placed efforts over further — the profile fits the dominant scenario well.
runners_data.comment: Won on her handicap debut last time, landing a close decision off a mark 3lb below today's — a consistently placed filly who has rarely been far away in recent starts. First-time cheekpieces worn and a trainer in form; effective over today's trip on a sound surface. The slightly higher mark is the only query.

runners_data.name: Thenandnow
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's three-year-old won on soft over six furlongs and has shown she handles good-to-firm (5th of 5f at Goodwood); Shane Foley takes the ride for a stable in good form at 6/42 over 14 days, and as a confirmed prominent type in role she is positioned to benefit if the pace is honest and controlled.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated on our figures and effective over today's distance on this going, she was beaten in a Listed event last time where the class of opposition was simply too strong. The move back into handicap company looks the right call; the breeding suggests more to come, and she is the selection.

runners_data.name: Soulful Diva
runners_data.note: Has been off 285 days, a notable absence that must be respected; David Marnane's filly won on good ground over five furlongs and Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride, but the step up to six furlongs on return and the lengthy lay-off both present questions — she is in role as a prominent type but needs to show she retains her zip.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a lengthy absence of over nine months, her win earlier in her career has been boosted by subsequent events, though she may be slightly flattered by the associated form. Most effective over five furlongs, today's six may test her stamina; there is a straightforward fitness question on her comeback.

runners_data.name: Treasured Royal
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's three-year-old is a natural prominent racer whose true style is front-of-field, yet the compressed field means she has been pushed back on the map because the real estate at the front is spoken for; her headgear (hood, previously raced in h) and a sim-going record of 1W2P in 9 are notes of interest, but she is likely to be racing out of her comfort zone positionally.
runners_data.comment: Second in our ratings and handles good ground well — her third at Down Royal last time could be excused if the conditions were softer than ideal. First-time hood applied; effective at today's trip, and the more suitable surface here gives her the chance to show her true ability. A strong danger.

runners_data.name: Beauty Queen
runners_data.note: A hold-up filly by profile with a headgear flag (previously ran in p); her form reads -68707 and the sim-going figures show 0W0P from seven comparable starts — N G McCullagh rides for Gerard O'Leary, but nothing in the profile suggests she is well-placed to exploit this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Struggling for form throughout recent starts, beaten seven lengths at Cork last time; the handicapper has eased her mark, giving her a fresh opportunity. She handles today's distance and surface, and first-time cheekpieces may help — improvement is required on current showing to land this.

runners_data.name: Girl Bear
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners a genuine hold-up type who has been off 51 days; running primarily over seven to eight furlongs and switching to six furlongs is a concern, but her placed effort over eight furlongs on good ground at least confirms she handles the surface — she needs pace to collapse in front of her which this shape may not fully provide.
runners_data.comment: Showed promise on her handicap debut, finishing third beaten just over two lengths off a mark fractionally above today's. Off a short break; today's going is quicker than she's shown her best on, and a notable jockey booking adds interest. More needed to land this.

runners_data.name: Hugo's Girl
runners_data.note: Thomas Dowling's four-year-old is a true hold-up horse whose natural rearward position has been compressed onto the map at midfield because the rear rank is crowded; Jack Cleary (5) rides and her best form on good ground (0W4P in 15 comparable starts) shows consistency without winning — the style-fit discount applies and she may again find herself in the wrong part of the race.
runners_data.comment: A near-miss last time, going down by just three-quarters of a length off a lower mark at Navan — she was back in form and handles today's trip. The mark has risen slightly, and a stiffer pace test than last time could bring the best out of her.

runners_data.name: Reimagined
runners_data.note: Nathan Crosse partners the most credible in-role closer in the field; the Daniel McLoughlin filly won over six furlongs on good ground (1/6f/GOO) and has solid placed form in similar conditions — as a genuine hold-up type she needs the pace to quicken and the gap to open, but her going and distance credentials are the strongest among the rear-division runners.
runners_data.comment: Third at this track last time when dropped in grade, showing better form after a difficult spell; could build on that. Effective at today's distance on this ground; first-time hood and blinkers applied — a significant gear change — and she could add to that latest effort.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Eagles
runners_data.note: A six-year-old veteran for Thomas Dowling wearing a tongue-strap (tp); won over six furlongs on good ground and placed three times in similar conditions giving a sim-going record of 1W3P, but being a true hold-up horse whose natural position is compressed onto the midfield map means she faces a positional challenge — Chris Hayes rides and the experience factor is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Back in form after winning recently, and third last time off this same mark where she was held up too long at a shorter trip. Today's distance is more suitable; she handles this going and carries a light weight. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces applied; inconsistency is the main reservation.

races.paceDynamic: Tropical Retreat is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead at the same odds of positioning, she should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop on good-to-firm ground over six furlongs at Fairyhouse. Glory To Be, Treasured Royal, Treasure Rose, Thenandnow and Soulful Diva are all natural prominent types, but with five horses competing for three or four front-rank slots, several will be shuffled back from their preferred position — the map absorbs Glory To Be and Treasured Royal into midfield precisely because the berths simply do not exist. This dynamic creates a race run at a sensible, even tempo rather than a scorching pace — Tropical Retreat setting the terms without being pressured means the pace is sustainable, and horses racing close to it will conserve more energy than in a contested early burn. The shape strongly favours prominent racers who are in role and close to the pace, and horses with a clean passage to track the leader rather than late closers having to make up ground in a race that will not fall apart up front. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural position, with Tropical Retreat, Treasure Rose, Thenandnow and Soulful Diva most likely to actually hold the front-rank slots, while Glory To Be and Treasured Royal face a race that may not suit them as well as the map implies.

watchPoints.text: Treasure Rose and Thenandnow are both in-role prominent types with strong form — watch for either or both of them travelling conspicuously well as Tropical Retreat sets the pace, as a one-two from the front-rank group is a genuine danger.

Glory To Be was racing just four days ago and is a natural front-of-field horse now expected to race in midfield — watch her early behaviour from the gates as any instinctive lunge for the lead could spike the tempo and reshape the entire race.

Soulful Diva has not run for 285 days; despite Dylan Browne McMonagle in the saddle, the lengthy absence combined with a step up in trip means she could be ring-rusty early — watch how she loads and travels in the first furlong.

Reimagined is the hold-up horse with the strongest going-and-distance profile and represents the primary threat to the prominent-dominated shape; if the pace is even marginally faster than anticipated, watch her making ground on the outside in the final two furlongs as the most likely closer to land a blow.

Treasured Royal's hood headgear and instinct to race prominently mean she could push forward aggressively despite the map placing her in midfield — if she does reclaim her natural position, track the effect on Tropical Retreat's ability to dictate.

races.name: Racing Again July 8th Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Carrigans Grove
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground 28 days ago and has the profile of a horse who wants to be handy; Gary Carroll will look to use that recent winning freshness from a prominent pitch, but this 7f trip on good-to-firm may just stretch her stamina in a strong-run race.
runners_data.comment: Back on the last mark off which she landed a handicap, Carrigans Grove handles today's trip and ground well, and first-time blinkers add interest. She was set to challenge at The Curragh last time but couldn't find extra, beaten seven and a half lengths.

runners_data.name: Little Miss P
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up filly stepping back to 7f after a series of longer-trip efforts; visor fitted, but the sim-going record (0 wins, 1 place from 6) on similar ground is thin, and a 44-day break adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Out of form throughout the season and operating below her best on current evidence, today's quicker ground could also be against her. The first-time visor and a top booking in the saddle are in her favour.

runners_data.name: Queen Aethelflaed
runners_data.note: In excellent form — won over 1m on good going 13 days ago, trainer Andrew Slattery has returned 4 winners from 33 runners over the past 14 days; Orla Tynan claims 7lb, distance drops to 7f which suits, and she maps naturally just behind the pace where the race shape is most favourable.
runners_data.comment: Won at Gowran Park two starts ago and clearly in decent fettle, though she went too keenly last time and paid for it, beaten five lengths off 67. First-time tongue-tie may help her settle; the mark asks slightly more this time.

runners_data.name: Are You In Or Out
runners_data.note: Won over 6f good ground recently and has multiple wins/places on similar going; Robert Whearty partners a horse who likes to race prominently, and the step back up to 7f from 6f winners' form is the main question mark.
runners_data.comment: Won at this track two starts back and handles today's trip on a sound surface, now 4lb higher than her winning mark that day. Last time she was well below form up in class, but course form is genuine and she can contest if back to her best.

runners_data.name: Famed Again
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who has finished 5th, 5th, 7th in her last three at this trip; 44 days off and a trainer with no runners in the 14-day window — hard to find a compelling angle here.
runners_data.comment: Pulled too hard and seemingly needing the outing when beaten eight lengths last time back after a break — she's been tried at a high level and her best form is on softer ground than today. Yet to score in recent starts, she needs to leave that reappearance effort behind.

runners_data.name: Hasita
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter for J P Murtagh whose trainer has been in strong form (7/33 T14); tagged with a style-fit flag because she races out of her most natural comfort zone stepped into a lead role, but she is still the one with most influence over tempo — the race revolves around how long she can sustain it.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated on our figures and making a handicap debut off a lenient opening mark — her maiden form has been boosted by subsequent Group-level success from rivals. Placed in her last two starts and effective over today's trip, she looks the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: Placed twice from 15 good-ground runs and is in consistent form off a 12-day turnaround; a natural prominent type who will want to press up from the gate, but the crowded early positions may push her slightly wider than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just a half-length off this same mark last time and handles today's trip and conditions well; the form suggests she arrives in good order. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces applied. A longstanding maiden is the reservation.

runners_data.name: Rodeeve
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground 19 days ago and clearly has ability on this surface; naturally a hold-up performer, nudged toward midfield on the map, meaning the trip stepping to 7f and the likely wider draw in a large field both need to fall right before her finishing kick becomes relevant.
runners_data.comment: Won here last time despite encountering interference, claiming a handicap by three and a half lengths off a mark 12lb below today's figure. She handles any surface and likes this track, but the substantial rise for that win is the key test; first-time cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Sagasti
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners a 3-year-old who has placed on good ground at 7f; a true hold-up type with a visor, and the sim-going record is sparse (2 from 5 similar) — needs the race to set up genuinely fast to get involved late.
runners_data.comment: Placed third at Gowran Park last time, beaten a length and a half off a slightly lower mark; she's clearly capable of going close. A tendency to race too freely is the main concern, and the first-time visor could help address that; acts on a sound surface over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Jasmine Affanalis
runners_data.note: Has placed twice on good ground at 8f and is held-up in her natural style, though pushed into a midfield slot here; the drop in trip from recent 8f runs could sharpen her, but the 21-runner field makes finding a clean path on the turn a significant ask.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced at Limerick last time after being seriously hampered on the home turn, which masked her true ability — prior to that she was running consistently well. First-time cheekpieces applied; handles today's trip on a sound surface, and on a fair mark from draw three.

runners_data.name: Mo Anam Chara
runners_data.note: Won over 1m on good ground and shaped well on a big-track surface; back to 7f now which may bring her speed to the fore, and racing from a prominent position suits — one of the more interesting tactical profiles in the race.
runners_data.comment: Landed a claiming event at Roscommon last time after a drop in class on her reappearance, winning by a length and a quarter. Back in handicap company now, she handles today's trip and has shown consistent ability; the key is whether she can reproduce that level in this stiffer contest.

runners_data.name: Two And Two
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on a synthetic surface and maps prominently; the step up to 7f turf good-to-firm is unproven territory, and the form at this distance is limited, making her a horse to watch in-running rather than press.
runners_data.comment: Found wanting at a short trip last time, failing to pick up when the pace quickened, though today's longer distance may bring out more. Inconsistent in her career so far; handles heavy and artificial surfaces, and today's quicker ground is a potential concern.

runners_data.name: Caitouna
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride on a 3-year-old who finished 4th on good-to-firm 28 days ago; true hold-up style, sparse sim-going record (0 wins, 0 places from 4), and needs everything to align in a big field.
runners_data.comment: Her handicap debut at The Curragh last time fell well short of expectations, beaten almost ten lengths. A drop to today's 7f may help if the mile was too far previously, and there's a notable jockey booking; otherwise more improvement is needed.

runners_data.name: Wild Berries
runners_data.note: Flags a tendency to fade in the finish, which is a significant concern in a 7f good-to-firm race where the tempo is unlikely to collapse; Siobhan Rutledge partners a filly whose recent form is consistently towards the rear of the field.
runners_data.comment: Off the back of what looked like a fitness run at The Curragh last time, she has solid two-year-old form that the handicapper has rewarded with a fair mark. Yet to show it in handicap company so far, though today's trip and ground are in her favour.

runners_data.name: Elly Bay
runners_data.note: Has placed three times from 9 similar-going runs and clearly handles good ground at 7f; naturally a front-pressing type that is forced toward midfield given the crowded prominent group, and at only 128lbs carries a weight advantage that could matter if the pace-pressers collide early.
runners_data.comment: Back to her best at this track last time, going down by just a half-length off a 1lb lower mark — a strong piece of form. Second on our ratings and clearly in good order; first-time cheekpieces added. She could improve with a stiffer pace, though today's ground is quicker than ideal.

runners_data.name: Imnotleavinyou
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce claims 3lb on a filly whose last five runs feature three 2nd-place finishes — a consistent performer, but genuinely hold-up in style and placed into midfield; the 7f on good-to-firm suits, but clean passage in a 21-runner field remains the key obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Won at Limerick two starts back off a mark 7lb below today's and matched her level when fifth last time off 62 — the same rating she carries today. On the up and handles today's trip; first-time tongue-tie applied, though the current mark asks slightly more.

runners_data.name: Bear Right
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes over on a John Harrington-trained 3-year-old who has placed at 8f on good and heavy; the trainer has been firing in winners (6/42 T14), but Bear Right is a natural prominent type remapped to midfield due to pace congestion — Foley's positioning skill becomes critical.
runners_data.comment: Given a clear opportunity at Cork last time, running to her rating in fourth beaten seven lengths. She's coming into form and handles today's trip, though her best going tends to be on softer ground than today's good-to-firm.

runners_data.name: Casla's Eagle
runners_data.note: Only three career runs with no wins or places; unproven on good-to-firm and the unknown style (U) is a genuine handicap for analysis in a field this competitive.
runners_data.comment: Showed promise in maidens before a short break and now tries handicap company for the first time. Drawn on the inside in a big field and acts over today's trip; more improvement needed on current figures to land this.

runners_data.name: Bundle Of Interest
runners_data.note: Highest-weighted runner at 144lbs and a genuine hold-up type; recent form is moderate (0 from last 5) and 53 days off for a McCreery yard that has returned 0 from 17 in the last 14 days — hard to make a case.
runners_data.comment: Her Naas outing looked like a fitness run, beaten nine lengths; she's had a short break since and steps back out with a first-time visor. Handles this trip, though acts best with more give than today's good-to-firm.

runners_data.name: Altimara
runners_data.note: Also 144lbs and has won twice on good-to-firm going; maps prominently which suits the race shape, though dropping back to 7f from recent longer-trip efforts is the key question — the sim-going record (2 wins, 3 places from 15) is the best going-profile in the field.
runners_data.comment: Progressive last year but out of form in recent starts, with last time's poor showing partly attributed to an unsuitably short trip. Back at a more appropriate distance today and usually held up for a late run; first-time hood applied, though the mark may still be slightly beyond her current form.

runners_data.name: Dervo Annie
runners_data.note: Won over 6f good ground and placed at 7f good; a natural prominent type squeezed to midfield by the pace logjam — if she can find a position closer to the pace than the map suggests, her in-form profile (1 win, 2 places from 7 similar) becomes more interesting.
runners_data.comment: Won at this track two starts ago off a mark 6lb below today's, and she handles the course well. Last outing in softer conditions over a longer trip saw her below form; back on the same rating here, better going and the return to today's trip could bring out a better effort.

races.paceDynamic: Hasita is the confirmed front-runner and, on a flat Fairyhouse 7f on good-to-firm ground, she is likely to find a comfortable rhythm without being seriously pressured from the gates — J P Murtagh's filly has shown a pattern of racing prominently and the pace report confirms she will not be chased down early by a rival of equal intent. Behind her, a cluster of genuine prominent types — Altimara, Queen Aethelflaed, Carrigans Grove, Mo Anam Chara and Two And Two — will contest the early positions immediately behind the leader, creating a solid but not frantic gallop that rewards horses who can sit just off the pace and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs. The field contains considerably more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Elly Bay, Bear Right, Dervo Annie and, to a degree, Minaun View are genuine pace-pressing horses redistributed into the midfield picture because the prominent berths are simply full, making their chances dependent on a wider, more energy-costly route. This race shape — a sustainable, single-paced lead with a deep prominent group — strongly favours horses who can race close to the pace without fighting for it, track the leader economically, and produce a clean finish through the final furlong on good-to-firm turf.

watchPoints.text: Queen Aethelflaed is the horse to monitor from the gates — if Orla Tynan slots her smoothly into the pocket behind Hasita without having to race wide or use energy, she arrives at the business end in the best-possible position given her recent 1m winning form.

The 21-runner field with multiple redirected prominent types (Bear Right, Elly Bay, Dervo Annie) creates a high risk of early crowding and interference on Fairyhouse's 7f bend; any runner drawn wide who has to chase across could burn critical reserves before halfway.

Hasita carries a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 — if she is slower away than expected or J P Murtagh elects not to force the pace, the race loses its single controlling tempo and the shape becomes far more unpredictable for every scenario.

Altimara (144lbs) and Bundle Of Interest (144lbs) are both top weights at 5 and 4 years old respectively — watch how quickly they travel in the first half-mile, as top weights who are off the bridle early in a large field rarely win.

Mo Anam Chara won over 1m on good ground 44 days ago and is now running over 7f; if she has retained that freshness and Ronan Whelan can position her just off Hasita's shoulder, the step down in trip could sharpen rather than shorten her finishing effort.

races.name: GAIN The Advantage Series Handicap

runners_data.name: Only One Scobie
runners_data.note: Flynn yard is winless from 13 runs in 14 days and this filly carries a fade flag; her recent similar-going record of 2 from 9 without a win or place is damning, and 1m½f on fast ground looks likely to expose her stamina limitations again.
runners_data.comment: Winning by five lengths at Leopardstown two runs ago highlighted his ability, and while he faces a 7lb rise in the weights today, his latest third is best read with lenience — he went for home prematurely when dropped back in distance. Progressive on the right terms, he appeals as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Fortuity
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners a horse that has won and placed at this sort of trip on good ground; the critical point is there is nobody to push Fortuity off the front, but its style-fit score of 0.93 signals it is technically racing out of its most comfortable role — watch whether Foley tries to coast or is asked to stretch immediately.
runners_data.comment: Landed a half-length success here on her penultimate outing and returns to a mark just 4lb higher than that winning effort. Sixth last time out was consistent with her rating, and she handles 7f on this surface; first-time cheekpieces fitted, and with form holding up, the frame is a realistic target.

runners_data.name: Hippology
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's runner has a 57-day absence to overcome and its only good-ground starts produced a 16th and a 5th; the fade flag is a further concern, and nothing in its form suggests it can quicken on a fast surface in a race that may not suit a stayer type.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well down the field in his most recent maiden, he showed little but was visibly inexperienced and this looks an easier opening opportunity. He handles 8-10f with some cut and has been off 57 days; from a trainer with a strong record at the track, he could improve switching to handicap company.

runners_data.name: Avec Grand Plaisir
runners_data.note: Unclassified style gives Fahey's runner tactical flexibility — its best recent run was a third on good ground over 8f and Whelan can slot wherever suits; represents one of the more open tactical profiles in the race and could benefit from a compressing pace.
runners_data.comment: Third on handicap debut at Cork most recently, beaten 4½ lengths in decent shape after stepping down in grade — a solid if unspectacular introduction to the discipline. He likely stays 10f and handles this surface, though a performance upgrade is needed to get involved here.

runners_data.name: John La Bear
runners_data.note: Returned from 210 days off to win over 8f on standard, finishing well; tongue-tie applied and the hold-up style suits a gathering finish, but similar-going record shows no wins or places on turf-going that compares to today, and the layoff context means fitness is an unknown quantity.
runners_data.comment: His latest handicap at Dundalk produced an opening success — by 1¼ lengths off a mark 6lb below today's — and he could still be ahead of the assessor. The lengthy absence of 210 days is a concern, and the yard has struggled for winners lately, but first-time tongue-tie suggests connections are treating the return seriously.

runners_data.name: Love Orchid
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's filly has headgear (blinkers) on and an unclassified style suggesting she can vary her position; five recent runs on similar going produced no wins or places, and the step up from 7f/8f to 1m½f is a significant and untested jump.
runners_data.comment: Held at the back of the field in her last handicap at Roscommon, she has failed to make an impression in recent starts and has yet to score in her last five. First-time blinkers fitted, and she handles the range of going, but at the foot of our figures there is too much to prove.

runners_data.name: Jp's Express
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose natural home is at the rear, here mapped to midfield because the field is rear-heavy; Wesley Joyce (3lb claimer) takes the ride and the style-fit flag of 0.90 reflects that JP's Express will likely not get the clean late run it needs in a bunched, steadily-run race.
runners_data.comment: Pushed wide from an awkward stall in his latest handicap at Leopardstown, the finishing position overstates how badly he went. He handles 7f on cut ground and all-weather surfaces, though a recovery in form is needed to register any meaningful progress here.

runners_data.name: Kc Bear
runners_data.note: Colin Keane brings significant jockey quality to a horse that has won over 6f on standard and placed over 8f — it has the tactical nous and the rider to exploit any pace scenario; though a natural hold-up type forced wider into midfield by field composition, Keane's ability to find a position and time a run makes this one of the more interesting profiles.
runners_data.comment: Held up in his usual manner here last time, he met interference at a pivotal moment and was left needing to do far too much from off the pace — the 2¼-length defeat off a mark 1lb higher than today's reads better than it looks. Consistent and effective over this trip, he should have every chance with a clear passage.

runners_data.name: Kirkland Sioux
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle on the O'Brien second string; all four career starts have yielded 7ths or worse and similar-going record is 0 wins and 0 places from 3 runs on comparable turf — needs a significant career-best on an unfamiliar step up in trip.
runners_data.comment: Held at Limerick last time after a tardy start left her needing to work hard to get into the race, but her trainer has an excellent record at today's track. She handles 8-12f and acts on yielding ground, though today's distance may be on the shorter end of her range — a touch more pace might not suit.

runners_data.name: Avoca Woods
runners_data.note: Jack Foley's filly has run only three times and fades in finishes; a true hold-up type shifted forward on the map by field congestion, carrying a style-fit discount of 0.90, and the fade flag combined with a modest similar-going record of 1 from 3 without a win makes this an uphill task.
runners_data.comment: Down the field in his latest maiden at Dundalk, he has produced a consistently moderate level of form and steps into handicap company for the first time today. His breeding suggests staying distances may suit better — today's 8f trip could be shorter than ideal — and a marked improvement is required.

runners_data.name: Cisterna
runners_data.note: Has a win and two places from 14 runs on similar going — the best strike-rate on that metric in the field; a genuine hold-up type repositioned to midfield by the rear-heavy field, with the style-fit score of 0.93 the only caveat, and the 7lb claimer Adam Browne-Souza needs to find a clean passage.
runners_data.comment: Landed a narrow success at Roscommon three runs ago on a mark 5lb lighter than today's, and his latest fifth is best excused — he encountered trouble having been asked to cover too much ground up in trip. Back at today's mark and 6-7f looks his range; a fair each-way prospect if stamina holds up.

runners_data.name: Make The Tide
runners_data.note: McCreery yard is winless from 17 in 14 days; unclassified style and a record of three consecutive 6th, 6th and 8th finishes gives no platform for optimism, though the tactical flexibility at least means W J Lee can place him wherever the gaps appear.
runners_data.comment: Held at Leopardstown on her latest start in a manner suggesting she wanted a stiffer test, she handles 7-8f and goes well on soft and good ground. The booking of a leading track jockey is a positive, and she could well improve making her handicap debut — the opening mark is the question.

runners_data.name: Retro Gal
runners_data.note: De Bromhead runner with four consecutive 7th-or-worse finishes and all on going softer than today; a true hold-up horse rerouted into the midfield map by the crowd of closers, carrying a style-fit flag of 0.90, and the fast surface is an unexplored variable for a horse that has always run on cut.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Limerick on her handicap debut — she faded late over a trip that stretched her — but the signs suggest 7-8f should be more to her liking. The type to improve as she gains experience in handicap company, though the current evidence is limited.

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: Has a win on standard going but that was over 8f from front/tracking position — today's fade flag and a poor recent sequence including a 15th suggest very low confidence; the tongue-tie remains but the style-fit score of 0.91 underlines she is not in her natural position and the Flynn yard is cold.
runners_data.comment: Out of form at present, he was well down the field in his most recent handicap at Leopardstown having failed to land a blow. First-time tongue-tie fitted today, and while he drops below his last winning mark, the form figures suggest a sharp turnaround is needed to feature.

runners_data.name: Schoolyard Days
runners_data.note: Grassick's runner carries the lowest OR in the field at 50 and a fade flag; a hold-up type compressed into midfield by field structure with a style-fit discount of 0.90, and five recent runs at shorter trips with no win or place on any going make this very hard to recommend from any angle.
runners_data.comment: Beaten nine lengths at The Curragh last time in a fashion that suggested the trip was too far, she is more at home over 5-6f and the shorter range could bring out the best of her. First-time cheekpieces today, but she has yet to produce consistent form and improvement is required.

races.paceDynamic: Fortuity is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 15-runner field and, critically, faces no serious challenger for the lead — on good to firm ground over 1m½f at Fairyhouse, that translates to a controlled, unchallenged gallop that is unlikely to be truly searching in the early and middle stages. With Fortuity able to dictate terms uncontested, the tempo will be measured rather than hot, meaning the field will bunch behind and the finish is likely to compress into a short sprint from the home straight rather than a true test of stamina. Several horses tagged as redistributed — Kc Bear, Jp's Express, Cisterna, Avoca Woods, Dawn Flame, Retro Gal, and Schoolyard Days — are genuine hold-up types who cannot all sit at the rear in a field this size and will be shuffled into mid-division positions that partially suit them but are not ideal; of these, Kc Bear and Cisterna have the class and form to capitalise most if they do find daylight. The race shape — a lone leader setting a comfortable gallop on fast ground — decisively favours horses tracking in the prominent-to-midfield berths who can respond when Fortuity is challenged turning in, rather than true closers who need a strong pace to reel in the leader.

watchPoints.text: Fortuity with Shane Foley in front — if Foley is not challenged by the first two furlongs and settles into a controlled rhythm, the lack of any genuine pace pressure creates a significant front-running advantage that could be decisive on this fast ground.

Kc Bear with Colin Keane is the highest-quality jockey-horse combination among the hold-up/midfield pack — if Keane can slot just off the pace and find daylight two furlongs out, the horse's best form (a win and a place on standard) gives it a realistic winning profile.

Cisterna has the best similar-going strike-rate in the field (10 runs, 1 win and 2 places) but is relying on a 7lb claimer (Adam Browne-Souza) to navigate a 15-runner field from a non-natural position — watch how much room they get turning for home.

John La Bear reappears after 210 days off having won last time out; the tongue-tie and the Ross O'Sullivan angle on a returning winner is worth tracking in the parade ring for signs of well-being before discounting the layoff entirely.

The going is reported as Good to Firm across the entire card — any watering or change reported track-side before the 7:20 could slightly alter the premium on pace-holding ability, but as it stands fast ground tilts the shape firmly toward Fortuity and prominent trackers.

races.name: Early Bird Winter Festival Tickets At Fairyhouse.ie Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Bella Colombia
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a recent win over this exact 8f trip on Good at Southwell; stepping up to 1m½f is new territory, jockey W J Lee retains the ride, but the step in trip and just 44 days since last run gives her a chance if the race is run to suit late finishers.
runners_data.comment: Back to a workable mark, she shaped with more merit than her fifth at Roscommon suggests — beaten four lengths off a mark 2lb higher than today's — and handles 8f and this going well. A leading track jockey booked, she makes a confident appeal as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Blue Anthem
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner and the key pace-setter today; raced just one day ago which is a significant fitness concern, and its recent form reads a string of poor finishes, but an uncontested lead on Good to Firm could flatter it well beyond its rating.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last six outings, a turnaround is required, but his Roscommon eighth is best excused — he missed the break and met sustained interference throughout, which flatters to deceive the margin. Effective on a sound surface and handles the distance, a clear run today could show him in a better light.

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has faded in the finish on recent starts, and his best recent effort came over a shorter 9f on Good; headgear (tp) retained, trainer Flynn has a quiet 14-day record, and the step back from extreme distances may help but the fade flag is a recurring worry.
runners_data.comment: Placed third at Leopardstown 13 days ago on a mark just 1lb below today's, that effort signalling a return to his better level under a forceful ride. He handles this trip well and acts on good to firm; clearly in a more positive frame of mind, he could build further on that recent revival.

runners_data.name: Launch Time
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a course-going profile that suits today — won over 8f on Good and has repeatedly shown well from handy positions; Colin Keane takes the ride from a yard that has had no runners in 14 days, but the horse's natural position just off the pace is ideal for this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Landed a narrow success three runs ago on a mark 5lb lower than today's, and the form held up well until his latest ninth, which is best excused — he expended too much energy in the early stages from a wide stall. First-time cheekpieces fitted, and a pound below his most recent starting mark, he retains a realistic chance.

runners_data.name: Pete's Dream
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type who has been running at shorter 7-8f trips on soft or standard ground; the step up to 1m½f on Good to Firm is a meaningful jump in trip and ground, headgear unchanged, and trainer Slattery is in good recent form with 4 winners from 33, so fitness is not the doubt — the trip is.
runners_data.comment: Held his form when fourth at Down Royal a fortnight ago, beaten 4¼ lengths with no excuses at the weights — a result that matched his current level. He drops in the weights today and handles multiple surfaces, though further improvement is still needed to feature prominently.

runners_data.name: Famous Enough
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who found 2nd over 8f on standard at Dundalk and has course experience at this 9f+ range; top-plate headgear retained, trainer Foley quiet in the last fortnight, but the horse handles Good ground and is well drawn to take up a position just off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Beaten ten lengths at Leopardstown last time, though that effort over a longer trip raises questions about stamina — he is arguably better placed at 8-9f on a sound surface. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces fitted today, and a significant rebound is required before he becomes relevant.

runners_data.name: La Campanella
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who fades in the finish and has one piece of form on Good going from eight attempts on similar surfaces; headgear (p) retained, the 26-day break is not a concern for a lightly-raced 4-year-old, but the fade flag and poor good-ground record make it hard to frame a strong case.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 9½ lengths here last time after pressing on too enthusiastically when tried over a longer trip, the drop back to 8f makes more sense today. First-time cheekpieces fitted, though her recent form is modest and she has yet to score in recent starts — improvement is needed to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Pure Valour
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie worn, lightly raced with only three career starts and just one on ground anywhere near Good; the 57-day absence is notable, and with no win or place from its limited profile, it is difficult to project improvement without more evidence.
runners_data.comment: Comfortably held at Gowran Park last time — a performance that sits in a run of moderate efforts — she has yet to encounter conditions that suit. First-time tongue-tie fitted and shorter trips may be more to her liking, but she remains a big ask for a competitive handicap field.

runners_data.name: Believeth
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie applied; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is at the rear of the field — mapped into midfield purely because several closers are competing for the same limited space at the back, so it may not secure the cover it needs and the fade flag adds further doubt to its finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: On our figures she ranks among the leading contenders and clearly retains ability — she handles 8f and goes well on a sound surface, and first-time tongue-tie is fitted today. The concern is a run of poor recent efforts, and a noticeable change in form will be needed to justify market interest.

runners_data.name: Milverton
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist with a tongue-tie; best form over 10-13f rather than this shorter 1m½f, and its natural deep-closer style is compromised today by being forced into a more prominent position on the map — the STYLE_FIT flag and fade warning together make this a low-confidence runner.
runners_data.comment: Going in the handicap sphere having shown little in maidens, his most recent run at Down Royal ended well beaten after he pressed on too keenly early. A step up toward 10f looks more suitable — today's 8f trip is shorter than his likely best — and first-time tongue-tie alone is unlikely to bridge the gap.

runners_data.name: Heart Of Darkness
runners_data.note: Persistent closer who has finished out of the frame in five of his last six runs on Good or Standard ground; placed into midfield on the map as a redistribution of a true hold-up style, the p headgear is retained, but trainer McGuinness's busy yard (3/28 in 14 days) has not been firing with this horse specifically.
runners_data.comment: On our figures she sits third in this field, suggesting ability on the right day — she handles 7-8f and acts with cut in the ground, and first-time cheekpieces today is a worthwhile switch. The concern is a run of poor recent efforts, and she will need a sharp upturn to justify market interest.

runners_data.name: Tullyesker
runners_data.note: Returning from a 231-day layoff with only three career starts, all on slower or heavy surfaces — no Good-to-Firm form whatsoever; tongue-tie worn, and the extended absence combined with the fast ground and a natural hold-up style that cannot be accommodated cleanly in this field make it an outsider on multiple counts.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of over seven months follows a well-beaten effort in a maiden, and his pedigree suggests shorter trips could be more suitable than today's 8f. First-time tongue-tie fitted, but there is significant improvement needed before he features in a competitive handicap field.

runners_data.name: Rushford
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type over staying distances (10-18f) squeezed into a midfield map position; the step down to 1m½f is significantly shorter than his best trips, the blinkers are retained, and his going record of 0 wins from 15 similar-surface runs tells its own story about his likely impact today.
runners_data.comment: Down the field here on his most recent outing, he has been on a regressive trajectory in both codes and today's 8f trip looks well short of the 12-14f range at which he is thought most effective. First-time blinkers fitted, but much needs to go right.

races.paceDynamic: Blue Anthem is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 1m½f handicap at Fairyhouse and, racing on just one day's rest, will be sent forward to control matters from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground. Launch Time and Pete's Dream are genuine prominent types who will push forward to track Blue Anthem closely, creating a small lead group but no genuine pace duel — the tempo is therefore likely to be honest rather than frenetic, suiting those who can travel into the race without cover. The field holds considerably more hold-up and prominent types than the race map can accommodate at the rear: Milverton, Believeth, Tullyesker, Heart Of Darkness and Rushford are all true hold-up horses redistributed into a midfield cluster on the map because there is physically no room at the back for all of them; of these, Blue Anthem, Launch Time and Pete's Dream are best placed to secure their natural positions. A controlled, single-pace gallop over this flat mile-and-a-half on fast ground strongly favours prominent racers who can travel economically behind an uncontested leader and pounce from a close-up berth in the straight — hold-up horses will need cover that may not materialise and face a stern test of their finishing kick on ground quicker than ideal for deep closers.

watchPoints.text: Blue Anthem's one-day turnaround is a serious red flag — watch in the paddock for signs of fatigue or stress, as a dull coat or reluctant loading could signal this pace-setter will capitulate earlier than the map suggests, collapsing the entire lead scenario.

Launch Time with Colin Keane is the horse to track through the race — if Keane travels comfortably into second place rounding the home turn, this is the horse most likely to pounce on Blue Anthem and its position on the map is perfectly engineered for that move.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Milverton, Believeth, Heart Of Darkness, Tullyesker and Rushford — will all be hunting similar ground at the back early; watch for traffic trouble and bumping as they settle, because a horse that gets a clean passage in that group could emerge as a surprise value runner if the pace lifts.

Bella Colombia's stamina for 1m½f is unproven — monitor how W J Lee deploys her in the early furlongs; if she is pushed forward unusually early it may signal the team knows she needs to conserve energy rather than launch a late run, which would alter her scenario fit entirely.

Pete's Dream has run exclusively at 7-8f on Soft or Standard surfaces — this Good to Firm ground over a longer trip is a double unknown, and if he struggles to stride out in the first half mile it could compress the leading group and change the complexion of the race for Blue Anthem.

runners_data.name: Keep It Together
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old with genuine hold-up credentials and strong Going form (10/11 sim-going runs), but 224 days off and a fading-finish flag temper expectations sharply; a true rear-runner who will find herself further forward than ideal given the crowded back of the field.
runners_data.comment: Yet to show anything of note in either code, she has been down the field in recent hurdle races and offers no encouragement on the Flat. Hard to make a case at these weights.

runners_data.name: Kimy
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type whose best recent run was a third at 16f on Good, but she drops back to 14f and her last five starts show no wins and only one placing; 13 days since last run and fades late, likely to be outpaced if the gallop stays moderate.
runners_data.comment: An inconsistent maiden over hurdles with all still to prove on the Flat, she was well beaten when switching to this surface at Leopardstown last time. The 2m trip looks within range but there is plenty to demonstrate.

runners_data.name: Altura
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington three-year-old who showed only a seventh on Good at 10f on her sole start — her natural style is hold-up but the field dynamics will push her forward; Shane Foley is a key booking for a filly with obvious scope for improvement.
runners_data.comment: Held up before staying on from the rear in her only outing at Leopardstown, a positive debut effort despite being well beaten. Back after 11 weeks and bred to get further, stepping up in trip should suit with better expected.

runners_data.name: Cosmetic
runners_data.note: AP O'Brien-trained three-year-old with a hood, who has raced mainly at shorter distances on Soft/Heavy/Standard — the step up to 14f on Good To Firm is a significant unknown and her form figures (9-9-7-5-5) suggest she has been finding this level competitive.
runners_data.comment: Dropped away before staying on into fifth at Cork last time, coping with the longer trip and showing stamina as her strong suit. Wears first-time cheekpieces and looks to be on the upgrade for an excellent yard; each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Essential Comedy
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old for Claire O'Connell with Colin Keane aboard — sixth over 13f on Good last time suggests she handles the conditions, but her running style is unknown and she has the look of a filly still learning her trade.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 6 lengths on debut at Leopardstown over 13f against competitive rivals, form that carries merit given the quality of the company. She has a top jockey in the saddle, though seeing out the full distance here is the key question.

runners_data.name: French Blond
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell filly who finished eighth over 10f on Good on debut — she is a natural hold-up type who will struggle to get to the back of this field and the fading-finish flag alongside limited stamina evidence makes the step to 14f a real question mark.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on her only start at Naas, where she made no impression and showed plenty of inexperience. The pedigree suggests middle distances suit and a step up in trip could unlock improvement; much still to prove, however.

runners_data.name: Invincible Destiny
runners_data.note: Second Harrington runner, wearing blinkers for the first time here; a single start over 12f on Heavy produced a 12th and she will be further forward than she'd prefer given the redistribution dynamic, which adds positional uncertainty to an already thin form profile.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well clear in her only start at Cork, a display that offered scant encouragement, though she is with a capable yard. The breeding crosses pace and staying ability, so experience should bring development in time.

runners_data.name: Path To Peace
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner with headgear (tv), going OK on Good, and W J Lee in the plate — two starts at 10f on Soft/Good have produced 10th and 9th but the critical factor is her absolute freedom to control pace from the front at a longer, more suitable trip.
runners_data.comment: Set too strong a pace before fading at Leopardstown last time, and a major step forward is required to feature here. She goes in first-time tongue-tie and visor with a top local jockey, and the pedigree points to a sounder surface suiting.

runners_data.name: Pleased
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride for Joseph O'Brien on a filly with a consistent 2-3 profile over 12f on Good — she appears to have a genuine prominent/midfield style that suits a moderate-pace scenario and her stamina looks reliable at the 14f extension.
runners_data.comment: A close second at The Curragh latest in a solid 12f outing that reflects well on her connections and pedigree. A trainer with an excellent record at this track takes the reins, and there should be more ahead from a filly with those credentials.

runners_data.name: Soigne
runners_data.note: Cromwell's second runner, a fader over 10f on Good on debut — any chance here depends on the step up to 14f unlocking improvement, but there is no evidence yet that the longer trip will suit and her one run showed no notable late momentum.
runners_data.comment: Showed considerable rawness in her only start at Naas, where she made no impression and was well beaten. Back after nine weeks, her breeding targets middle distances and improvement is possible as she gains experience; much still to demonstrate.

runners_data.name: Spry
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed for McConnell with no published form, going UNKNOWN, and a tongue-tie noted — the absence of any evidence makes her impossible to assess with confidence, though unexposed three-year-olds at this trip occasionally outrun their lack of profile.
runners_data.comment: A debutante by Teofilo out of Something Graceful, herself a thoroughly useful performer at middle distances, and half-sister to Sometimesadiamond, smart at 7f — a pedigree pointing toward 1m4f. The trainer is currently out of form and she will likely need the experience.

runners_data.name: Vanir
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh-trained filly with a second at 10f on Good to her name — Ben Coen has good form for the yard and she handles the going well; the step up from 10f to 14f is the key question but her prominent style and Good-ground consistency give her a solid profile in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just half a length at Gowran Park latest, a display that left the clear impression she needed a longer trip. She acts on yielding ground, her trainer is in excellent form, and stepping up in distance here looks to play to her strengths.

runners_data.name: Werifesteria
runners_data.note: Third Harrington runner, hood-wearing, with only a seventh over 12f on Standard to show — the switch to Good To Firm turf over a longer trip is a significant ask and she will need a big step forward from her debut performance.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on her only start at Dundalk, a debut that left questions unanswered, but she is in capable hands and the US pedigree suggests 1m-plus suits. First-time cheekpieces applied; a sounder surface should also help, and better is likely to follow.

races.paceDynamic: Path To Peace is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, critically, faces no pressure for the lead — she will settle into a comfortable, owner-controlled gallop on Good To Firm ground over 1m4f with W J Lee able to dictate entirely on her own terms. The pace is unlikely to be strong; a lone leader who can control tempo from the front on fast ground at this trip creates a race that compresses the field and makes it very difficult for deep hold-up horses to generate the momentum needed to reel her in late. The field nominally contains many hold-up types, but Keep It Together, Invincible Destiny, French Blond, and Cosmetic are all redistributed runners who cannot actually secure their natural rear positions — the map is crowded at the back and several will be forced to race closer than they'd like. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield racers with proven finishing ability over 12f+ on Good ground, as a moderate uncontested pace rewards those who can travel economically close to the leader and quicken briefly in the straight rather than those relying on a truly strong gallop to set up a late burst.

watchPoints.text: Path To Peace (W J Lee) jumping cleanly and finding the lead — if she installs herself in front unchallenged within the first two furlongs, the race is effectively hers to control and give away.

Pleased (McMonagle/JPO'Brien) settling in a prominent position — if she travels smoothly 2-3 lengths off Path To Peace through the middle sections, she becomes the most dangerous challenger as the field straightens for home.

Vanir (Ben Coen/Murtagh) — watch her position at the half-mile mark; if she is within 4 lengths of the leader at that point on Good To Firm ground she will be a serious factor, but if she gets shuffled back she faces a very different task.

Multiple redistributed hold-up types (Keep It Together, Invincible Destiny, French Blond, Cosmetic) will be jostling for position in the early stages — any crowding or interference in the first 3f could disrupt the running order and create a more pressured tempo than Path To Peace would prefer.

Spry is completely unknown — if she breaks well and takes up an unexpected prominent position, she could inject pace into the race and materially change the dynamic that currently heavily favours Path To Peace's lone-leader scenario.
